g.text: LM training stages: pretrain → mid → post
Modern language model training proceeds through distinct stages: pretraining
on internet-scale data to acquire world knowledge, mid-training on curated
corpora to extend capabilities, and post-training to shape model behavior
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=3) Modern language model training proceeds through distinct stages: pretraining on internet-scale data to acquire world knowledge, mid-training on curated corpora to extend capabilities, and post-training to shape model behavior (Guo et al., 2025; Team OLMo, 2025; Yang et al., 2025).

g.text: For reasoning-focused models, post-training typically begins with supervised
fine-tuning (SFT) on long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) demonstrations, often
distilled from more capable models, where reasoning traces can span
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) For reasoning-focused models, post-training typically begins with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) demonstrations, often distilled from more capable models, where reasoning traces can span thousands of tokens before reaching a final answer.

g.text: SFT primes for downstream RL stages
This SFT step, analogous to behavioral cloning in reinforcement learning
(Osa et al., 2018), primes the model for subsequent stages such as
reinforcement learning from human feedback (Ouyang et al., 2022) or
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=4) This SFT step, analogous to behavioral cloning in reinforcement learning (Osa et al., 2018), primes the model for subsequent stages such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (Ouyang et al., 2022) or reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (Guo et al., 2025; Shao et al., 2024).

g.text: long-CoT data is expensive to obtain
Unlike pretraining data, which can be scraped at scale from the web,
high-quality long-CoT demonstrations require either expensive human
annotation or careful distillation from larger models, including generation,
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) Unlike pretraining data, which can be scraped at scale from the web, high-quality long-CoT demonstrations require either expensive human annotation or careful distillation from larger models, including generation, filtering, and validation of long reasoning traces.

g.text: how to best use limited SFT data matters
As a result, the question of how to best utilize limited SFT data is
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=0) As a result, the question of how to best utilize limited SFT data is practically important.

g.text: common assumption: more unique samples is better
The common assumption in machine learning would suggest that training with
more unique training samples yields better generalization.
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=0) The common assumption in machine learning would suggest that training with more unique training samples yields better generalization.

g.text: theory: generalization bounds improve with size
Under i.i.d. sampling, each new example provides independent information
about the data distribution, and generalization bounds in statistical
learning theory typically improve with dataset size.
g.title: N7 [Context] (cites=0) Under i.i.d. sampling, each new example provides independent information about the data distribution, and generalization bounds in statistical learning theory typically improve with dataset size.

g.text: This principle manifests practically throughout the field – data
augmentation techniques are widely used to artificially expand effective
dataset size when real data is limited (Hernández-García & König, 2018;
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) This principle manifests practically throughout the field – data augmentation techniques are widely used to artificially expand effective dataset size when real data is limited (Hernández-García & König, 2018; Shorten & Khoshgoftaar, 2019), and the success of large language models has been attributed in significant part to training on ever-larger unique corpora.

g.title: N9 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Following this logic, modern post-training pipelines employ millions of SFT samples (Team OLMo, 2025).

g.text: more epochs on smaller data wins under fixed budget
Under a fixed update budget, training for more epochs on smaller datasets
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) Under a fixed update budget, training for more epochs on smaller datasets outperforms training on larger datasets.
N12 [Result] (cites=0) The gains are not marginal.

g.text: perf + termination rate co-scale with epochs
The performance and termination rates, i.e., the model’s ability to
successfully conclude reasoning with a final answer, both scale with epoch
count and saturate together, suggesting that sufficient repetition of the
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) The performance and termination rates, i.e., the model’s ability to successfully conclude reasoning with a final answer, both scale with epoch count and saturate together, suggesting that sufficient repetition of the same data is required for models to fully internalize the demonstrated reasoning structure.

g.text: We find that this convergence is tightly linked to training set
g.title: N14 [Result] (cites=0) We find that this convergence is tightly linked to training set memorization.

g.text: Performance improvements plateau once models achieve near-perfect next-token
prediction accuracy on the training data, even as validation loss continues
g.title: N15 [Result] (cites=0) Performance improvements plateau once models achieve near-perfect next-token prediction accuracy on the training data, even as validation loss continues to rise.

g.text: This relationship holds across all models we test, all benchmarks, and
different training datasets, making train token accuracy a practical
g.title: N16 [Result] (cites=0) This relationship holds across all models we test, all benchmarks, and different training datasets, making train token accuracy a practical stopping criterion for scaling epochs.

g.text: Despite this apparent overfitting, we observe no additional catastrophic
forgetting compared to single-epoch training on large datasets.
g.title: N17 [Result] (cites=0) Despite this apparent overfitting, we observe no additional catastrophic forgetting compared to single-epoch training on large datasets.

scaling epochs on smaller datasets substantially
g.title: N18a [Contribution: Phenomenon] (cites=0) We demonstrate that under a fixed update budget, scaling epochs on smaller datasets substantially outperforms scaling unique samples.

g.text: We identify training token accuracy as a reliable
stopping criterion for epoch scaling, with performance
gains plateauing once models reach full memorization,
and we show that multi-epoch training on small datasets…
g.title: N18b [Contribution: Dynamics] (cites=0) We identify training token accuracy as a reliable stopping criterion for epoch scaling, with performance gains plateauing once models reach full memorization, and we show that multi-epoch training on small datasets causes no additional catastrophic forgetting compared to large datasets.

g.text: We show how training data properties, such as teacher
model size in distillation and the correctness of data
g.title: N18c [Contribution: Factors] (cites=0) We show how training data properties, such as teacher model size in distillation and the correctness of data samples, affect the repetition advantage.

g.title: N19 [Contribution] (cites=0) While we provide a practical heuristic for exploiting the repetition advantage, we pose explaining this phenomenon in long-CoT SFT as a novel, open problem for the community.
